Results and Discussion Charge/Discharge Cycles: Figure 24 shows the bulk sulfur temperature as a function of time during the cold start operation as sulfur was heated from its frozen state to molten state (sulfur melting point: 118-119 oC). The bulk sulfur temperature in Figure 24 was calculated as the average of all internal thermocouples. The temperature contour illustrated in Figure 24 was obtained by cubic spline interpolation method of sulfur temperature measurements obtained from the internal thermocouples located at different spatial points. The black circles in the contour map represent the internal HTF pipe circuits and 6” charge pipe (see Figure 20 and 21). The dashed line denotes the fill level of molten sulfur in the vessel. Figure 25 shows bulk sulfur temperature and temperature measured at two different locations inside molten sulfur TES obtained for seven charge/discharge cycles. The calculated heat rates are shown in Figure 26. During the daily cyclic operation, sulfur TES was charged at a peak charge rate of 4 kWt. In cycle 5, a cloud transient stop-start event was conducted as seen by the steep decline and increase in heat rate during charge process. Figure 27 shows the charge and discharge duration for the seven thermal cycles. It can be observed that the charge and discharge duration for all the cycles was ≤ 10 hours and ≥ 14 hours, respectively. Figure 28a elucidates the temperature measured by different internal thermocouples during cycle #7 and a snapshot of the cross-sectional temperature contour. Figure 27a shows that there is negligible variation in the axial temperature of molten sulfur during the transient charge and discharge process (compare temperature measured by thermocouple z = +14.3” and z = -46.4”). This trend suggests the activity of natural convection currents within molten sulfur. Figure 27b shows the measured HTF inlet and exit temperature during the discharge process.
